info.title: Raven TUI RPC
info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 contract between the Raven Python parent process (RpcServer) and the Node TUI child process (RpcClient). Single source of truth for both sides. Pydantic v2 models in raven/rpc/models.py and codegen-derived TypeScript types in ui-tui/src/rpc/generated.ts must stay in sync with this file. Drift is caught in CI by tests/test_rpc_schema_match.py and `npm run lint:rpc`.

methods.name: dag.get
methods.summary: Read one run_subagent_dag run back off disk.

params.name: session_key
params.description: Scopes the registry rows consulted for an unfinalized run's overlay.

methods.summary: Read one DAG node's rendered prompt and output.
methods.description: Neither is carried by the graph: the manifest inlines only the leaf nodes' text, and the tool result kept in the transcript is clamped to 200 chars.

params.name: max_output_chars
params.description: Head of the output to return; the file itself is uncapped. Defaults to 20000.

params.name: session_key

BrowserRef.description: One actionable element, with the id a click can be aimed at.

value.description: Never present for a password field.

noop.description: True when nothing moved, including when the context engine owns compaction.

SessionInitInfo.description: The banner bundle: which model, which tools and skills, how full.

lazy.description: True when no agent loop was running, so tools/skills are empty.

tools.description: Tool names in a single 'builtin' bucket.

update_command.description: The command that would install the newer release.

config_notices.description: What a config migration changed on the user's behalf during this boot. Drained, so only the first session of a launch carries them.

endpoint.description: Which of a multi-endpoint provider's endpoints this session is on; null for single-endpoint ones.

SessionUsage.description:
``info.usage`` — the boot baseline, refreshed by each turn's completion.

Distinct from :class:`UsageSnapshot`, which is the per-turn event payload:
this one carries the context-window fill a banner draws, and its counters
are named for the session rather than for one LLM call.

context_estimated.description: True when context_used is a tiktoken estimate of a resumed transcript, not a measurement.

TranscriptMessage.description: One stored message in wire form: ``content`` renamed to ``text``.

reasoning_ms.description: How long the thought on this assistant entry took, measured server-side from the first reasoning delta to the first answer token or tool call. Absent means unknown (an unstreamed call, or a session written before it was recorded) -- render the bare header, never a zero.

duration_ms.description: How long the call this role='tool' entry answers ran, dispatch to result. Absent means unknown, same rule as reasoning_ms.

diff.description: A file tool's unified diff of the change it made, on its role='tool' entry.

TranscriptNotice.description: Marks an assistant entry the runtime wrote rather than the model.

kind.description: Which runtime decision this reports; `action_blocked` today.

TranscriptTurnEnded.description: Why a turn's transcript stops where it does.

arguments.description: JSON-encoded arguments; re-serialized when stored as an object.

hub.description: Installed from the skill hub, so skillhub.remove can uninstall it.

mcp_server.description: Owning MCP server, or null for a built-in tool.

needs.description: Set when the tool exists but is withheld for want of a key. The model cannot call it; the row is here so the page can offer the field instead of the tool simply being absent.

setting.description: Dotted config key that unlocks the tool.

model.description: Empty when the shipped placeholder is still in place.

api_key_set.description: Whether a key is stored; the value never goes on the wire.

set.description: Whether a value is stored; the value itself never rides the wire.

fields.description: Every field the channel takes, so a client can render its configure form.

running.description: Whether the adapter is up, read from the live gateway. Null when no gateway answered.

connected.description: Whether the account is paired. Only the QR-login channels report this; null means the channel does not report a pairing and must not be drawn as disconnected.

qr_login.description: Whether this channel signs in by scanning a code.

MemoryItem.description:
One row, projected card-sized. ``kind`` decides which optional fields
carry a value: the four memory types share only ``id`` and ``kind``.

PlughubCatalogItem.description: The card-sized projection of a catalogue entry.

transport.description: None when the entry contributes no MCP server.

kinds.description: Which contribution kinds the entry carries: mcp, skill, python.

McpSnapshot.description:
One server's live connection state, as `MCPConnectionManager` reports it.

Every mutating `plug.*` call answers with this, and the gateway broadcasts the
same shape as an `mcp.status` notification, so a client renders one state
machine rather than two.

PlugLedger.description: What the install actually landed, which is what uninstall replays.

pieces.description: One entry per landed piece: {kind: 'mcp', server} or {kind: 'skill', name, skillhub_id}.

installed_name.description: The local directory name when installed, else empty.

JsonValue.description: Recursive JSON value type. Implemented as an unconstrained object in JSON Schema; downstream Pydantic uses typing.Any.

SessionListItem.description: One row in the TUI session picker (gatewayTypes.ts SessionListItem).

pinned.description: User pinned this session to the top of the picker.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the tool's input arguments.

id.description: A spawn's call id, or '<run_id>/<node>' for a graph node. Opaque to a client: a spawn row opens through subagent.context and a dag row through dag.node, which is what kind is for.

kind.description: spawn | dag. Which delegation path made this, and so how it is opened.

run_id.description: dag rows only: the graph run this node belongs to.

node.description: dag rows only: the node's id inside that run.

label.description: What it was asked, in short.

status.description: run | ok | error | cancelled | queued | skipped. The last two only occur for graph nodes.

agent.description: The external agent that ran it, or null for a raven subagent.

instance.description: The handle sharing one stateful agent session, if any.

started_at.description: ISO 8601; the record stores epoch millis.

ended_at.description: Absent while it is still running.

message_count.description: What was asked, plus the answer once there is one.

tokens.description: Input plus output tokens this run spent. Null, not zero, when the transport that ran it cannot report usage -- the cli lane never can.

tool_call_count.description: How many tools it called. Null where the transport has no per-step visibility.

upgrade_to.description: The transport this entry's preset has since moved to, or null when it is current. A configured entry is never rewritten underneath the user, so the mismatch is shown instead.

model_labels.description: Keyed by the model id as it appears in `models`.

ModelLabel.description: How a model reads to a person. Absent for a model no catalogue knows -- one released since the bundled snapshot, or served by a local deployment -- in which case the id is all there is to show.

ProviderEndpointInfo.description: One of a provider section's several url/key groups. `label` is the idempotency key the write methods address an entry by.

DirectTarget.description: One sub-agent instance a turn is addressed to. Null means the main conversation.

InstanceRow.description: One sub-agent instance this session has used, verbatim from the instance registry. camelCase because the web RPC serves the same record unchanged. `runId` / `nodeId` are set only on a dag-node row.

DirectTurn.description: One side of one direct-chat turn, read back from its record directory.

stdout.description: Rich-rendered output with ANSI SGR sequences.

stderr.description: Error / warning output with ANSI SGR sequences.

error_code.description: Only present for timeout / not-dispatch-compatible cases (mirrors a JSON-RPC error code).

error.description: Human-readable explanation of why this method is not supported in v0.1.

hint.description: Optional hint to the user (e.g., 'Press Ctrl+C').

canon.description: alias (with leading /) -> canonical mapping. v0.1: alias = canonical 1:1 (no short aliases generated; TS-side prefix-1-match handles partials). Group + subcommand are space-separated (e.g. '/channels status'), not slash- or dot-separated.

pairs.description: Ordered (alias, canonical) tuples. TS-side createGatewayEventHandler.ts:198 gates on non-empty pairs; empty pairs degrades to slash.exec direct dispatch.

sub.description: group -> [subcommand]. Blacklisted entries (e.g. channels login) and agent-REPL are filtered out.

categories.description: Ordered category list: '(top-level)' first then alphabetical group names. Fully filtered groups (e.g. tui) do not appear.

skill_count.description: Total skill count from skill_forge store SQL count; 0 if DB missing (warning field then populated).

warning.description: Optional warning pushed to TUI activity strip (e.g. 'skill store not initialized').

payload.description: `target` names the conversation this event belongs to; absent is the main agent.

content.description: The message that started the turn. Present so a client that did not send it can draw the question: the user entry reaches the transcript only at turn end.

NoticeEvent.description:
Prose the runtime wrote, not the model.

It must not arrive as `token.delta`: that buffer is the model's voice, so the text would render as the answer -- glued to whatever the model narrated just before it, carrying the answer's copy and branch actions, and stuck in English whatever language the turn was in.

kind.description: Which runtime decision this reports; `action_blocked` today.

detail.description: The blocking tool's own first line, when it gave one.

diff.description: Unified diff of what the call changed on disk, when the tool could produce one.

SubagentDeliveredEvent.description: A delegated run's result re-entered its conversation here. The injection itself is invisible on the wire -- the next frame a client sees is an assistant turn nobody visibly asked. Emitted just after the result is submitted to the main loop, so a client can mark the seam where the sub-agent's answer came back.

label.description: The spawn's display label, or the dag's run_id.

run_id.description: Set for kind=dag, so a client can open the run.

DagNodeStatus.description: Per-node status reported by the DAG runner. 'interrupted' never comes off the wire -- it is what a client infers for a node still called running when the run stopped reporting.

DagSnapshotNodeStatus.description: Per-node status in a run read back off disk. Unlike the event vocabulary this includes 'interrupted', which the server infers for a node the registry still calls running on a run nothing is executing.

DagRunSnapshot.description: One run rebuilt from its run dir. 'finalized' is false while it is still executing, in which case per-node state came from the instance registry overlay rather than a manifest.

DagNodeDetail.description: One node's rendered prompt and the head of its output. Either text is absent when its file does not exist: a node that never ran has no prompt, a failed one no output.

status.description: This node's own last recorded status; null when the run has written no manifest yet.

error.description: Why the node failed. A failed node has no output, so without this it reads as unanswered.

DagRunStartedEvent.description: A run_subagent_dag call accepted a graph. Carries the whole topology so a client can lay the graph out before any node reports.

tool_call_id.description: The call this run belongs to. Absent on hosts that do not correlate progress with a tool row.

instance.description: Shared stateful handle. Nodes naming the same one run sequentially.

DagRunCompletedEvent.description: The run finished. Terminal node output text is deliberately absent -- it is already in the tool result.

TurnEvent.description: Discriminated union of turn streaming events. The 'type' field is the discriminator.
